nodes.description: OER performance in acidic electrolyte (0.5 M H2SO4) using three-electrode system
nodes.source_text: The OER performance of various catalysts was evaluated using a three-electrode system in 0.5 M H2SO4 conditions at 25°C. The overpotential of the Co3O4/Ni-RuO2/rGO was as low as 195 mV at a current density of 10 mAcm−2. The Co3O4/Ni-RuO2/rGO shows overpotentials of only 249 and 305 mV when the current density is increased to 50 and 100 mAcm−2, respectively. The Tafel slope of Co3O4/Ni-RuO2/rGO is derived as 41.4 mVdec−1. The Co3O4/Ni-RuO2/rGO and Co3O4/RuO2/rGO have Cdl values of 5.99 and 5.67 mFcm−2, respectively.

nodes.description: Chronopotentiometric stability test at multiple current densities
nodes.source_text: To evaluate the stability of the Co3O4/Ni-RuO2/rGO we conducted chronopotentiometric measurements at the current densities of 10, 50, and 100 mA cm−2. Notably, all current densities show insignificant changes over the 10 h test, validating the outstanding stability of Co3O4/Ni-RuO2/rGO during OER.

nodes.description: Long-term stability test at 100 mA/cm2 in acidic electrolyte
nodes.source_text: The Co3O4/Ni-RuO2/rGO catalyst could be effectively maintained for 100 h at 100 mAcm−2, whereas the performance of RuO2/rGO, Co3O4/RuO2/rGO, and Ni-RuO2/rGO shows ≈60% decay after 8, 20, and 32 h, respectively.

nodes.description: Cyclic voltammetry stability test with 2000 and 5000 cycles
nodes.source_text: The LSV curves indicate that the overpotential of the Co3O4/Ni-RuO2/rGO catalyst increases by only 8 mV (2000th cycle) and 10 mV (5000th cycle) after CV cycles between 1.0 and 1.5 V (vs. RHE) at a current density of 50 mA cm−2.

nodes.description: OER performance in alkaline electrolyte (1 M KOH)
nodes.source_text: The overpotential and Tafel slope of the Co3O4/Ni-RuO2/rGO are 210 mV (10 mAcm−2), 75.5 mVdec−1 in 1 M KOH conditions.

nodes.description: OER performance in neutral electrolyte (1 M PBS)

nodes.characterization_summary: X-ray diffraction shows the as-synthesized Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO is composed of cubic-phase Co₃O₄ (JCPDS 43-1003) and rutile RuO₂ (JCPDS 43-1027), with Ni contents in RuO₂ following the same rutile structure due to low content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) spectra show that the as-synthesized Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO is composed of cubic-phase Co₃O₄ (JCPDS 43-1003) and rutile RuO₂ (JCPDS 43-1027, Figure S3), wherein the Ni contents in RuO₂ follow the same rutile structure due to the low content.

nodes.characterization_summary: Field emission scanning electron microscopy shows Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂ particles uniformly grown on rGO surface with average size of 8.99 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the field emission scanning electron microscopy and TEM images, the Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂ particles are uniformly grown on the rGO surface, having an average size of 8.99 nm (Figures 1b and S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: Transmission electron microscopy images confirm Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂ particles uniformly grown on rGO surface with average size of 8.99 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the field emission scanning electron microscopy and TEM images, the Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂ particles are uniformly grown on the rGO surface, having an average size of 8.99 nm (Figures 1b and S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy shows two distinctly different lattice interfaces of Ni-RuO₂ and Co₃O₄, demonstrating formation of Ni-RuO₂/Co₃O₄ heterojunctions with lattice fringe spacings of 0.28 nm (Co₃O₄ {220}) and 0.25 nm (RuO₂ {101}).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HAADF-STEM image shows that two distinctly different lattice interfaces of Ni-RuO₂ and Co₃O₄ were observed, further demonstrating the formation of Ni-RuO₂/Co₃O₄ heterojunctions (Figure 1c). Specifically, the lattice fringe spacings are derived as 0.28 and 0.25 nm, which can be indexed into the Co₃O₄ {220} and RuO₂ {101} planes, respectively (Figure 1c,d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected high-angle annular darkfield scanning transmission electron microscopy demonstrates formation of Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂ heterojunction with Ni uniformly doped into RuO₂ lattice, confirmed by intensity profile showing sudden intensity drop due to lower atomic mass of Ni relative to Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HAADF-STEM image shows that two distinctly different lattice interfaces of Ni-RuO₂ and Co₃O₄ were observed, further demonstrating the formation of Ni-RuO₂/Co₃O₄ heterojunctions (Figure 1c). The corresponding intensity profile also demonstrates that Ni is doped into the RuO₂ lattice, wherein the sudden intensity drop was due to the presence of Ni atom with a lower atomic mass relative to Ru (Figure 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Energy dispersive spectroscopy mapping of Co, Ru, Ni, and O shows the interface of Co₃O₄/RuO₂ heterojunction can be resolved while Ni is uniformly dispersed into the RuO₂ lattice.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) mapping of Co, Ru, Ni, and O in the complex, the interface of Co₃O₄/RuO₂ heterojunction can be resolved while Ni is uniformly dispersed into the RuO₂ lattice (Figure 1e,f).

nodes.characterization_summary: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analysis of Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO shows Co 2p peaks at 779.8 and 795.1 eV indicating Co oxides, with approximately 0.4 eV negative shift compared to Co₃O₄/rGO attributed to electron transfer from Ni-RuO₂ to Co₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co 2p spectrum of Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO shows two characteristic peaks at 779.8 and 795.1 eV, respectively, suggesting the existence of Co oxides (Figures S5 and S6a). Specially, compared to the Co₃O₄/rGO, the Co 2p peaks for Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO indicate an approximately 0.4 eV negative shift, which is attributed to the electron transfer from Ni-RuO₂ to Co₃O₄.

nodes.characterization_summary: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy Ni 2p spectrum of Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO shows two peaks at 855.5 eV (Ni 2p₃/₂) and 872.2 eV (Ni 2p₁/₂), validating successful doping of Ni into RuO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Ni 2p spectrum of Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO (Figure S6b) shows two peaks at 855.5 eV (Ni 2p₃/₂) and 872.2 eV (Ni 2p₁/₂), validating the successful doping of Ni into RuO₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy Ru 3d spectra show binding energies of Ru 3d₅/₂ at 280.5 eV and 3d₃/₂ at 284.6 eV for Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO, positively shifted by roughly 0.2 eV relative to pure RuO₂/rGO, indicating higher oxidation state of Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Regarding Ru 3d XPS spectra, the binding energies of Ru 3d₅/₂ (280.5 eV) and 3d₃/₂ (284.6 eV) for Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO are positively shifted for roughly 0.2 eV relative to pure RuO₂/rGO (Figure S6c), suggesting that the Ru element in the Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO heterojunction has higher oxidation state than in RuO₂/rGO.

nodes.characterization_summary: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy O 1s peak shows three characteristic peaks corresponding to lattice oxygen (529.8 eV), oxygen vacancies (531.2 eV), and surface adsorbed O (532.6 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The O 1s peak shows three characteristic peaks after deconvolution, which correspond to the peaks for lattice oxygen (529.8 eV), oxygen vacancies (531.2 eV), and surface adsorbed O (532.6 eV, Figure S6d).

nodes.characterization_summary: X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectroscopy at Co K-edge reveals valence states of Co in Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO are lower than those in pure Co₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra and absorption threshold reveal that the valence states of Co in the Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO complex are lower than those in Co₃O₄ (Figure S7).

nodes.characterization_summary: Extended X-ray absorption fine structure Fourier-transformed k³-weighted spectrum in R-space reveals Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO has two characteristic peaks at 1.50 Å (Co-O) and 2.42 Å (Co-O-Co), consistent with pure Co₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the Fourier-transformed k³-weighted extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectrum in R-space reveals that the Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO has two characteristic peaks at 1.50 Å (Co-O) and 2.42 Å (Co-O-Co), which are consistent with pure Co₃O₄.

nodes.characterization_summary: X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectroscopy at Ni K-edge shows Ni oxidation state in Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO is very close to NiO, suggesting Ni²⁺ valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XANES and absorption threshold revealed that the Ni oxidation state in Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO is very close to NiO, suggesting a Ni²⁺ valence state (Figures 2a and

nodes.characterization_summary: Extended X-ray absorption fine structure Fourier-transformed spectrum in R-space reveals Ni K-edge shows R positions at 1.54 Å (Ni-O) and 2.61 Å (Ni-Ru bonds), demonstrating successful doping of Ni atoms into RuO₂ lattice.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FT-EXAFS spectrum in R-space reveals that the R position of Ni is at around 1.54 and 2.61 Å, corresponding to the Ni-O and Ni-Ru bonds, respectively (Figure 2b). The observation of Ni-Ru and Ni-O bonds demonstrates the successful doping of Ni atoms into the lattice of RuO₂ in Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO.

nodes.characterization_summary: X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectroscopy at Ru K-edge shows valence of Ru atoms in Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO is lower than that of pure RuO₂, with valence state decreasing gradually across Co₃O₄/RuO₂/rGO, Ni-RuO₂/rGO, and Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru K-edge XANES and absorption threshold plots revealed that the valence of Ru atoms in Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO is lower than that of RuO₂ (Figures 2d and S10). The valence state of Ru decreases gradually in the Co₃O₄/RuO₂/rGO, Ni-RuO₂/rGO and Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO, indicating that it is more favorable for electron transfer from Ni to RuO₂ in Ni-RuO₂/rGO relative to Co to RuO₂ in Co₃O₄/RuO₂/rGO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Extended X-ray absorption fine structure Fourier-transformed spectrum at Ru K-edge shows characteristic peaks of Ru-O bond (1.50 Å) and Ru-Ni bond (2.45 Å), confirming Ni doping in RuO₂ with Ru bonding to six O and one Ni atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, the characteristic peaks of the Ru-O bond (1.50 Å) and Ru-Ni bond (2.45 Å) were also resolved in the FT-EXAFS spectrum, confirming the Ni doping in RuO₂ (Figure 2e). The fitting results of Ru in Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO further demonstrated Ru bonding with six O and one Ni atoms (Figure 2f and Table S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Linear sweep voltammetry shows Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO achieves ultra-low overpotentials of 195 mV at 10 mA cm⁻², 249 mV at 50 mA cm⁻², and 305 mV at 100 mA cm⁻², significantly outperforming RuO₂/rGO, Ni-RuO₂/rGO, and Co₃O₄/RuO₂/rGO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 3a, the linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves exhibit that the Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO heterojunction significantly outperforms RuO₂/rGO, Ni-RuO₂/rGO, and Co₃O₄/RuO₂/rGO in terms of current density. Specifically, the overpotential of the Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO was as low as 195 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm⁻², remarkably lower relative to the commercial RuO₂ (333 mV, Figure S11a), RuO₂/rGO (311 mV), Ni-RuO₂/rGO (285 mV), and Co₃O₄/RuO₂/rGO (415 mV, Figure 3b). Especially, the Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO shows overpotentials of only 249 and 305 mV when the current density is increased to 50 and 100 mA cm⁻², respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Tafel slope analysis shows Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO has Tafel slope of 41.4 mV dec⁻¹, much lower than RuO₂/rGO (366.3 mV dec⁻¹), Co₃O₄/RuO₂/rGO (134.6 mV dec⁻¹), and Ni-RuO₂/rGO (98.3 mV dec⁻¹), indicating faster OER kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Tafel slope of Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO is derived as 41.4 mV dec⁻¹, much lower than 366.3 mV dec⁻¹ (RuO₂/rGO) 134.6 mV dec⁻¹ (Co₃O₄/RuO₂/rGO), and 98.3 mV dec⁻¹ (Ni-RuO₂/rGO) indicating faster OER kinetics (Figure 3c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Cyclic voltammetry analysis shows electrochemical double-layer capacitance (Cdl) of Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO is 5.99 mF cm⁻², much higher than Ni-RuO₂/rGO (4.31 mF cm⁻²) and RuO₂/rGO (3.08 mF cm⁻²), suggesting presence of Co₃O₄ sites enhances active surface area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical double-layer capacitance (Cdl) was calculated based on the cyclic voltammetry (CV) plots (Figure S13) in the potential range of 0.2-1.2 V at the scan rates from 20 to 120 mV s⁻¹. As shown in Figure 3d, the Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO and Co₃O₄/RuO₂/rGO have Cdl values of 5.99 and 5.67 mF cm⁻², respectively, much higher than those of Ni-RuO₂/rGO (4.31 mF cm⁻²) and RuO₂/rGO (3.08 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy tests confirm Tafel slope results, showing Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO has superior charge transfer kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Tafel slope results are consistent with the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy tests (Figure S12).

nodes.characterization_summary: Chronopotentiometric measurements at current densities of 10, 50, and 100 mA cm⁻² show insignificant changes over 10 h test, validating outstanding stability of Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO during OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To evaluate the stability of the Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO we conducted chronopotentiometric measurements at the current densities of 10, 50, and 100 mA cm⁻². Notably, all current densities show insignificant changes over the 10 h test, validating the outstanding stability of Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO during OER.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cyclic voltammetry cycling between 1.0 and 1.5 V (vs. RHE) at 50 mA cm⁻² shows overpotential of Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO increases by only 8 mV after 2000 cycles and 10 mV after 5000 cycles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The LSV curves indicate that the overpotential of the Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO catalyst increases by only 8 mV (2000th cycle) and 10 mV (5000th cycle) after CV cycles between 1.0 and 1.5 V (vs. RHE) at a current density of 50 mA cm⁻² (Figure S14).

nodes.characterization_summary: Transmission electron microscopy image after 2000 CV cycles indicates Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO catalyst has excellent stability in 0.5 M H₂SO₄ conditions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the TEM image and EDS mapping after 2000 CV cycles indicated that the Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO catalyst has excellent stability in 0.5 M H₂SO₄ conditions (Figures S15 and S16).

nodes.characterization_summary: Long-term chronoamperometric i-t test at 100 mA cm⁻² shows Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO maintains performance for 100 h, whereas RuO₂/rGO, Co₃O₄/RuO₂/rGO, and Ni-RuO₂/rGO show approximately 60% decay after 8, 20, and 32 h respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 3g, the Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO catalyst could be effectively maintained for 100 h at 100 mA cm⁻², whereas the performance of RuO₂/rGO, Co₃O₄/RuO₂/rGO, and Ni-RuO₂/rGO shows ≈ 60% decay after 8, 20, and 32 h, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy after i-t cycling test for 20 h at 100 mA cm⁻² shows retention ratios of Ni and Ru in Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO are 87.2 and 94.4 wt%, respectively, much higher than 78.1 and 84.8 wt% in Ni-RuO₂/rGO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ICP-AES results indicate that the retention ratios of the Ni and Ru in the Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO catalyst were 87.2 and 94.4 wt%, respectively, after the i-t cycling test for 20 h at 100 mA cm⁻², much higher than 78.1 and 84.8 wt% in the Ni-RuO₂/rGO catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy Ru 3d binding energy shows only 0.1 eV positive shift after 20 h i-t cycling test, demonstrating insignificant oxidation of RuO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The binding energy of Ru 3d XPS spectra has only 0.1 eV positively shifted after the 20 h i-t cycling test, further demonstrating the insignificant oxidation of the RuO₂ (Figure S18).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman spectroscopy shows RuO₂/rGO exhibits characteristic Eg (489.3 cm⁻¹), A1g (595.8 cm⁻¹), and B2g (796.4 cm⁻¹) vibration modes that diminish gradually as potential increases from 1.3 to 1.8 V, attributed to increased Ru valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 4e,f, both catalysts show characteristic Raman peaks of Eg (489.3 cm⁻¹), A1g (595.8 cm⁻¹), and B2g (796.4 cm⁻¹) vibration modes for the RuO₂/rGO and Co₃O₄/Ni-RuO₂/rGO. When the applied potential was increased from 1.3 to 1.8 V, the three peaks diminished gradually for RuO₂/rGO, which was attributed to the increased valence state from Ru³⁺/⁴⁺ to Ru⁴⁺/⁶⁺, and further to Ru⁶⁺/⁸⁺.
